In general, we can see that the distribution of cost benefit ratios is smaller as the number of tariff components that are dynamic increases. For example, Level 2 EV has a much tighter distribution of cost benefit ratio in the Full tariff scenario than the Mild. In the cost benefit ratio calculation, the cost of technologies that enable dynamic pricing response is the same across all tariff scenarios for each analysis year as described in the previous section. However, bill savings is different in each tariff scenario with the largest bill savings accruing in the Full tariff followed by the Medium and Mild tariff scenarios. As a result, the cost benefit ratio tends to decrease as we move from Full to Medium to Mild tariffs. This trend is consistent across end uses. 41 Figure 27. Distribution of cost benefit ratio across end uses for each tariff design scenario in 2030 low price forecast 3.4.3 Payback period Figure 28 shows the distribution of payback periods across the entire customer base for each end use. In this figure, the x-axis denotes the cumulative number of customers with a payback period equal or lower than the value on the y-axis. (Refer to Section 2.5 for details of the definition of payback period and the formula used to calculate it). The figure shows the distribution on three separate panels, one for each sector - residential, commercial, and agricultural. We ignore all entries with negative payback periods resulting from bill savings that cannot recover even the O&M and financing costs. We can also see that there are a significant number of customers in most end uses with payback period equal to 0, particularly in the Full tariff design scenario (top row of figures). These are the customers that already have the technology installed and therefore have no up-front costs to pay back. On the Full tariff, almost all EV customers pay off their technology in less than one year, indicated by the nearly flat magenta lines that bend up at a sharp angle as a few outliers with very long payback periods bring up the tail end of the curve. On the Mild tariff, this is still true, though there are more customers with payback periods between 1-2 years. Residential pool pumps and water heaters show similar payback period trends; on the Full tariff, nearly all 42 customers have paid off the technology in 1-2 years, while the Mild tariff has a significant amount of 3-5 year payback periods. Spa pumps have very low loads and are assumed to use the same technology (at the same cost) as pool pumps; while this can still be paid off in 4-10 years on the Full tariff, it is generally not ever going to be cost effective on the Mild.
